mainTopic: Wage arrangements and ריבית, acquiring flax, and when a sale of wine or oil becomes final
overview: The amud opens by finishing a ברייתא about hiring a worker cheaply for harvest time. The גמרא uses it to challenge רב and שמואל, but רבא answers that lowering wages is not real ריבית. The only problem is how it looks, and that depends on whether the worker starts working right away. Next, רב ששת explains how cutting a little flax can acquire all of it: the seller told the buyer to clear some land and acquire everything on it. A new משנה then teaches that a sale of wine or oil becomes final when the measuring vessel is filled. It also says a middleman bears the loss of a broken barrel, and the seller must drip three extra drops for the buyer. The גמרא asks whose measuring vessel this is, and רבי אילעא answers that it belongs to a סרסור. Finally, רבי אלעזר seeks out רב's student to raise a difficulty about the drained drops, and his objection continues on the next amud.

steps.title: End of the ברייתא about hiring a worker for harvest
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rules that hiring a worker for harvest at a low wage is forbidden. Hiring him starting today at a fixed daily wage that also covers harvest is permitted.
steps.simpleTranslation: If at harvest a day's work is worth a סלע, it is forbidden to benefit from him. But if he hired him starting today for a דינר a day, and at harvest the work is worth a סלע, it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing a ברייתא it started quoting just before. It is setting up a challenge against רב and שמואל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first case, the worker agrees now to work at harvest for a low wage, which is forbidden. In the second case, he is hired starting today at one steady daily wage, and that is allowed even though harvest work is worth much more.

keyTerms.meaning: Threshing floor; here it means harvest time, when workers are in high demand
A smaller silver coin; one quarter of a סלע
Forbidden to benefit from him, meaning to hire him on these terms

phrases.english: and at the threshing floor [a day's work] is worth a sela —
it is forbidden to benefit from him.
But if he hired him from today
for a dinar a day,
and at the threshing floor it is worth a sela — it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלַגּוֹרֶן יָפֶה סֶלַע אָסוּר לֵהָנוֹת הֵימֶנּוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the ברייתא the גמרא started quoting just before
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hiring only for harvest at a low wage is forbidden. Hiring from today at a steady daily wage that includes harvest is permitted.

steps.title: Challenge to רב and שמואל from the second case
steps.stepSummary: If each unit counts as a separate deal, as רב and שמואל hold, then each harvest day should be a separate cheap deal and should be forbidden. So why does the ברייתא permit it?
steps.simpleTranslation: If you think that in 'a כור for thirty, a סאה for a סלע', each unit is bought separately, then here too each day is priced on its own, and it should be forbidden. Yet the ברייתא permits a דינר a day when harvest work is worth a סלע. Why? Isn't it payment for 'wait for me'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב and שמואל. Under their approach, the permitted case in the ברייתא should really be forbidden.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב and שמואל say a price set 'per unit' makes each unit its own deal. Applied here, each harvest day would be its own underpaid deal, just like the forbidden first case. The second case is permitted only if the whole period is one deal, and that suggests 'per unit' pricing does not split a deal apart.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it enters your mind; introduces an idea in order to disprove it
A large measure, equal to thirty סאה
He acquires each one, one by one
Payment for 'wait for me'; a reward for an early deal, which looks like ריבית

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not against the ברייתא. It is against רב and שמואל: the ברייתא's lenient ruling only makes sense if the days are not separate deals.

phrases.english: And if it enters your mind
"A kor for thirty,
a se'ah for a sela I am selling you" —
he acquires each first one, one by one;
phrases.notes: This is the view of רב and שמואל: each סאה is bought as soon as it is measured.

phrases.english: here too —
he fixed the price for each one, one by one,
phrases.notes: He means each day of work is priced on its own.

phrases.english: and it should be forbidden to benefit from him;
yet [when hired] for a dinar a day
and at the threshing floor it is worth a sela — it is permitted?!
Why?
But it is payment for "wait for me"!
phrases.notes: The worker takes less pay in exchange for an early deal, and that looks like ריבית.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the ברייתא just quoted to challenge רב and שמואל
steps.kashyaTarget: רב and שמואל's rule that 'per סאה' pricing makes each unit a separate acquisition
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If each day were a separate deal, each harvest day would be underpaid and forbidden, like the first case. The ברייתא permits it, so the days must not be separate.

steps.title: רבא: lowering wages is not truly forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רבא rejects the premise of the question: agreeing to work for less is not real ריבית at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Do you really think so? Is it forbidden to lower one's price in hiring?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא pushes back on the challenge. He says a worker taking lower pay is not real ריבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge assumed that underpaying at harvest is truly forbidden. רבא says a worker may accept less to secure a job; that is not interest. So the question built on that assumption is weakened.

keyTerms.meaning: And do you really think so? Rejects an assumption
Lowering the price of hired work

phrases.english: Rava said:
And do you really think so?!
Lowering [the price] in hiring —
is it forbidden?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the assumption behind the challenge in step 2
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The premise that underpaying a worker is real ריבית
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Lowering wages is not truly forbidden, so the question cannot depend on true ריבית

steps.title: Then why are the two cases different?
steps.stepSummary: If lowering wages is allowed, why does the ברייתא forbid the first case and permit the second?
steps.simpleTranslation: What is different about the first case, and what is different about the last case?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks the natural follow-up question. If lowering wages is allowed, why is the first case forbidden?
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא's claim seems to permit both cases. So the גמרא needs a reason why the ברייתא treats them differently.

keyTerms.meaning: The first part of a source
The last part of a source

phrases.english: What is different about the first clause
and what is different about the last clause?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי שְׁנָא רֵישָׁא וּמַאי שְׁנָא סֵיפָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows from רבא's claim, which seems to erase the difference between the two cases
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the ברייתא distinguishes between the two cases if lowering wages is allowed
steps.kashyaTarget: רבא's claim that lowering a worker's wage is not forbidden
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If lowering wages is permitted, the ברייתא should permit the רישא as well, yet it forbids it. So there must be some difference between the two cases.

steps.title: It depends on whether the worker starts now
steps.stepSummary: In the first case the worker does not start working now, so the deal looks like 'wait for me' payment. In the second case he starts working now, so it does not look that way.
steps.simpleTranslation: In the first case, where he does not work with him from now, it looks like payment for 'wait for me.' In the last case, where he works with him from now, it does not look like payment for 'wait for me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the difference. The problem is only how it looks, and that depends on whether the work begins right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing here is real ריבית. When the cheap work happens only later, it looks like a reward for an early deal. When the worker starts now at one steady wage, it looks like a normal job, so it is permitted.
steps.whatToRemember: Hiring a worker cheaply is not real ריבית. It is forbidden only when it looks like a 'wait for me' reward, which happens when the work starts only later.

phrases.english: The first clause, where he does not work
with him from now,
it looks like payment for "wait for me";
the last clause, where he does work
with him from now,
it does not look like payment for "wait for me."

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא דְּלָא קָא עָבֵיד בַּהֲדֵיהּ מֵהַשְׁתָּא
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The difference is only appearance: work that starts later looks like a 'wait for me' reward, but work that starts now does not.
steps.whyThisMatters: Since the issue is only appearance, the ברייתא no longer proves anything about whether 'per unit' pricing splits a deal, so the challenge to רב and שמואל falls away.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the cases: the prohibition is only about appearance, depending on whether work starts now
steps.terutzHavaAmina: If lowering wages is permitted, there is no reason to forbid the רישא
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא is forbidden only because, with no work starting now, it looks like אגר נטר לי. The סיפא, where work starts now, does not look that way.

steps.title: Cutting any amount of attached flax acquires it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the line from the previous משנה: if the flax was still attached to the ground and the buyer cut any amount, he acquired it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if the flax was still growing in the ground and the buyer cut even a little of it, he acquired it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה so it can examine it. This sets up the question that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that cutting even a tiny bit of growing flax is enough for the buyer to own it. The wording sounds like the small cut acquires all of the flax, and that is what the גמרא is about to question.

keyTerms.meaning: Still attached to the ground, still growing
He detached, pulled up, or cut
Any amount at all, even a tiny bit
He acquired it, it now legally belongs to him

phrases.english: And if it was attached to the ground,
phrases.notes: This is talking about the flax from the previous משנה.

phrases.english: and he detached any amount – he acquired.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: Detaching any amount of attached flax acquires it.

steps.title: How can a small cut acquire all the flax?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the משנה: why should cutting just a little acquire all of the flax?
steps.simpleTranslation: Just because he cut a little, he acquired all of it?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is surprised by the משנה's rule and challenges it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An act of קנין normally acquires only what it is done on. Cutting a few stalks should acquire only those stalks, not the whole field of flax.

keyTerms.meaning: Just because, because of the fact that

phrases.english: Because he detached any amount – he acquired?!
phrases.notes: The surprise is that he gets all of the flax, not only the little bit he cut.

steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's rule that cutting any amount acquires the flax
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A קנין done on part of the flax should not acquire all of it.

steps.title: רב ששת: the seller said to clear land and acquire everything on it
steps.stepSummary: רב ששת explains that the משנה is talking about a seller who told the buyer: go clear any amount of land, and acquire everything on it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב ששת said: Here the seller told the buyer, 'Go clear a bit of land for yourself, and by doing that acquire everything that is on it.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב ששת answers the challenge by narrowing the משנה to a specific case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Cutting the flax clears a patch of ground. Because the seller said 'clear some land and acquire everything on it,' that clearing counts as a קנין done on the ground itself. Through it, the buyer acquires everything growing there, not just the few stalks he cut.

keyTerms.meaning: What case are we dealing with here? (used to narrow a source to a specific case)

steps.whatToRemember: Cutting a little flax acquires all of it only because the seller set up that act as the way to acquire: 'clear some land and acquire everything on it.'

phrases.english: Rav Sheshet said:
With what are we dealing here?
Where he said to him: Go,
clear for yourself any amount of land,
phrases.notes: Pulling up the flax clears and improves the ground, so the cutting itself is the land-clearing.

phrases.english: and acquire everything that is on it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שֵׁשֶׁת: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the משנה to a specific case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Cutting a little flax acquires all of it on its own
steps.terutzMaskana: It works only because the seller said: clear any amount of land and acquire everything on it

steps.title: New משנה: selling wine and oil, and the middleman's broken barrel
steps.stepSummary: If prices change before the measuring vessel is filled, the goods are still the seller's. Once it is filled, they are the buyer's. If a middleman's barrel breaks, the middleman takes the loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone sells wine or oil and the price goes up or down, then before the measure is filled the goods still belong to the seller, and once it is filled they belong to the buyer. If a middleman was between them and the barrel broke, it broke at the middleman's loss.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It teaches the exact moment a sale of liquids becomes final.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Filling the measuring vessel is the point when ownership passes to the buyer. Before that, either side can back out if the price changes. A סרסור who measures with his own barrel is responsible if it breaks.

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who sells wine and oil to his fellow,
and they rose or fell in price,

phrases.aramaic: אִם עַד שֶׁלֹּא נִתְמַלֵּאת הַמִּדָּה – לַמּוֹכֵר.
phrases.english: if before the measure was filled – it is the seller's.
Once the measure was filled – it is the buyer's.
And if there was a middleman between them,
and the barrel broke – it broke for the middleman.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A sale of liquids becomes final when the measuring vessel is filled, and a middleman bears the loss if his barrel breaks.

steps.title: The three extra drops, and who is exempt
steps.stepSummary: The seller must let three extra drops drip out for the buyer. Whatever he drains out afterward by tilting the vessel is his. A storekeeper is exempt, and רבי יהודה exempts everyone on ערב שבת near dark.
steps.simpleTranslation: The seller must let three more drops drip out for the buyer. If he then tilted the vessel and drained it, that is the seller's. A storekeeper does not have to drip three drops. רבי יהודה says: on ערב שבת as it gets dark, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with another rule about selling liquids: the extra drops owed to the buyer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After pouring, the seller must give the buyer the last three drops that drip from the measure. Anything beyond that, squeezed out by tilting the vessel, stays with the seller. The storekeeper, and according to רבי יהודה anyone in the rush before שבת, does not have to wait for those drops.

phrases.english: And he is obligated to drip for him three drops.

phrases.aramaic: הִרְכִּינָהּ וּמִיצֵּית – הֲרֵי הוּא שֶׁל מוֹכֵר.
phrases.english: If he tilted it and it was drained – it is the seller's.
phrases.notes: After the three drops, if he tips the measure to get the last bits out.

phrases.aramaic: וְהַחֶנְווֹנִי – אֵינוֹ חַיָּיב לְהַטִּיף שָׁלֹשׁ טִיפִּין.
phrases.english: And the storekeeper is not obligated to drip three drops.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
Shabbat eve at nightfall – he is exempt.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: A seller must drip three extra drops, except a storekeeper, and according to רבי יהודה anyone on ערב שבת at dusk.

steps.title: Whose measuring vessel is it?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who owns the measuring vessel mentioned in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This measuring vessel: whose is it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה with a clarifying question. This sets up the two options it will test next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Who owns the vessel matters, because goods placed into a person's own vessel can be acquired by him. The answer affects when the buyer should become the owner.

phrases.english: GEMARA: This measure – whose is it?

steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the measuring vessel belongs to the buyer or to the seller

steps.title: If it is the buyer's vessel, why wait until it is full?
steps.stepSummary: If the vessel belongs to the buyer, he should own the liquid as soon as it enters, even before the vessel is full.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is the buyer's measure, how can the משנה say it is still the seller's before the measure is filled? It is the buyer's own vessel!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the first option and shows that it clashes with the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A person's own vessel acquires for him whatever goes into it. So with the buyer's vessel, every drop should become his right away, and filling the vessel should not matter.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a possibility that will be rejected)

phrases.english: If we say it is the buyer's measure,
before the measure is filled – it is the seller's?!
It is the buyer's measure!
phrases.notes: His own vessel should acquire the liquid for him the moment it goes in.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the first possible answer to the question
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the measure belongs to the buyer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A buyer's vessel acquires immediately, so the משנה's 'before it is filled, it is the seller's' would make no sense.

steps.title: If it is the seller's vessel, why does filling it help the buyer?
steps.stepSummary: If the vessel belongs to the seller, filling it should not transfer anything to the buyer, since the liquid is still in the seller's vessel.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if it is the seller's measure, how can the משנה say it is the buyer's once it is filled? It is the seller's vessel!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests the second option and shows that it also clashes with the משנה. Both options now seem to fail.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Liquid sitting in the seller's own vessel has not yet reached the buyer. So filling it should not make the buyer the owner. The גמרא is left needing an answer that fits the משנה.

keyTerms.meaning: But rather (moves to the other option)

steps.confusionAlert: Both options are rejected here. Do not think the גמרא has settled on one of them. The next step gives the answer.

phrases.english: But rather, the seller's measure?
Once the measure is filled – it is the buyer's?!
It is the seller's measure!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests the second possible answer after the first was rejected
steps.kashyaTarget: The assumption that the measure belongs to the seller
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Liquid still in the seller's own vessel has not reached the buyer, so filling it should not transfer ownership.

steps.title: The measuring vessel belongs to a middleman
steps.stepSummary: רבי אילעא says the משנה is talking about a measuring vessel that belongs to a סרסור.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אילעא says: The משנה is talking about a measuring vessel that belongs to a middleman.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אילעא answers the question of steps 11-13. The vessel belongs to neither the buyer nor the seller. It belongs to a סרסור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the vessel were the buyer's, he would acquire the liquid right away. If it were the seller's, he would never acquire it. A third-party vessel avoids both problems. It is lent to the seller while it fills, and once it is full it is lent to the buyer.

keyTerms.meaning: Middleman, a broker between buyer and seller

phrases.english: Rabbi Ela says:
With a measuring vessel of a middleman.
phrases.notes: The vessel is the middleman's. He lends it to the seller, and once it's full it counts as lent to the buyer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the problem that neither owner works
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case: a third party owns the vessel
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The vessel must belong to either the buyer or the seller
steps.terutzMaskana: It belongs to a סרסור, so filling it can mark the moment of transfer

steps.title: The latter clause treats the middleman as a new case
steps.stepSummary: The סיפא brings up a סרסור as a new case, which suggests the רישא had no סרסור at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the latter clause teaches: 'If there was a middleman between them and the barrel broke, it broke for the middleman.' This implies that the first clause is not dealing with a middleman!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי אילעא from the wording of the משנה itself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The סיפא says 'and if there was a סרסור' as though adding something new. That means the רישא was not about a סרסור. So how can רבי אילעא explain the רישא as a סרסור's vessel?

keyTerms.meaning: The latter clause of a משנה
The first clause of a משנה

phrases.english: But from the fact that the latter clause teaches:
And if there was a middleman between them,
the barrel broke – it broke for the middleman;
it may be inferred that in the first clause
we are not dealing with a middleman!

steps.kashyaTarget: רבי אילעא's claim that the רישא involves a סרסור's vessel
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The סיפא introduces a סרסור as a new case, so the רישא must have had none

steps.title: The middleman's vessel versus the middleman himself
steps.stepSummary: The רישא has the סרסור's vessel without him there. The סיפא has the סרסור himself present at the sale.
steps.simpleTranslation: The first clause is about a middleman's measuring vessel without the middleman. The latter clause is about the middleman himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by telling apart the two clauses of the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both clauses involve a סרסור, but in different ways. In the רישא only his vessel is used. In the סיפא he is personally there handling the sale, which is why he takes the loss when the barrel breaks.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's measuring vessel belongs to a סרסור. In the רישא only his vessel is used; in the סיפא the סרסור is present himself and is responsible.

phrases.english: The first clause – a measuring vessel without the middleman,
phrases.notes: The vessel is the middleman's, but he isn't at the sale.

phrases.english: the latter clause – with the middleman himself.

steps.triggerLanguage: רֵישָׁא – מִדָּה בְּלֹא סַרְסוּר, סֵיפָא – בְּסַרְסוּר עַצְמוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the סיפא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting the two clauses into different cases
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The סיפא's mention of a סרסור means the רישא had none
steps.terutzMaskana: The רישא has only the סרסור's vessel; the סיפא has the סרסור himself present

steps.title: Quoting the משנה about tilting and draining
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה: liquid drained out by tilting the vessel belongs to the seller.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he tilted the vessel and drained it, that liquid belongs to the seller.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה to open a new discussion. This is a setup for what follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After the three drops, whatever the seller drains out by tilting the vessel is his. The coming story centers on a difficulty with this ruling.

phrases.english: He tilted it and drained it –
it belongs to the seller.

steps.triggerLanguage: הִרְכִּינָהּ וּמִיצֵּית – הֲרֵי הוּא שֶׁל מוֹכֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to a new line of the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Liquid drained by tilting the vessel belongs to the seller

steps.title: רבי אלעזר looks for רב's student
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר arrives in ארץ ישראל and asks זעירי who the תנא is that רב taught the laws of measures. זעירי points out רב יצחק בר אבדימי.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי אלעזר went up, he found זעירי and asked him: Who here is the תנא whom רב taught the laws of measures? זעירי showed him רב יצחק בר אבדימי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story. רבי אלעזר is looking for the person who learned these laws from רב, setting up his question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A תנא here is someone who memorized and recited teachings. רבי אלעזר wants to hear the exact wording from whoever learned it from רב.

phrases.english: When Rabbi Elazar went up,
phrases.notes: Went up from בבל to ארץ ישראל.

phrases.english: he found Ze'eiri,
he said to him: Who here is the tanna
whom Rav taught the laws of measures?
He showed him Rav Yitzchak bar Avdimi.

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי סָלֵיק רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, אַשְׁכְּחֵיהּ לִזְעֵירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Story introducing a question on the quoted משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is the תנא that learned the laws of measures from רב

steps.title: What is bothering you?
steps.stepSummary: רב יצחק בר אבדימי asks רבי אלעזר what his difficulty is.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: What is difficult for you?
steps.whatsHappening: רב יצחק בר אבדימי asks רבי אלעזר to explain his problem. This sets up the difficulty that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only invites רבי אלעזר to speak. The real content is the difficulty he is about to present.

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: רב יצחק בר אבדימי is speaking to רבי אלעזר.

phrases.english: What is difficult for you?

steps.title: רבי אלעזר begins his difficulty with the משנה
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר starts his difficulty by quoting the משנה: drained liquid belongs to the seller.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר answered that the problem is what we learned: If he tilted the vessel and drained it, that liquid belongs to the seller.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר starts to explain his difficulty by quoting the משנה. The difficulty itself continues on the next amud, so this step is a setup.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He repeats the משנה because his question is aimed at exactly this ruling. The full objection has not been stated yet.

phrases.english: That we learned:
phrases.notes: Now רבי אלעזר is answering, explaining what bothers him.

phrases.english: he tilted it and drained it –
it belongs to the seller,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers 'what is difficult' by quoting the משנה
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's ruling that drained liquid belongs to the seller
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Setup only; the full objection continues on the next amud
